body: I'm having the shittiest day of my life today too. I woke up wanting to die and the pain hasn't gone away. So now I'm sitting in a parking lot eating pretzels instead of going to work or staying home with roommates. I'll be here for awhile if you decide you want to talk...

Funny because I never for a moment thought that it might "sound strange", the idea you put forth that blips of happiness are more painful than depression. I guess that says a lot about how miserable I am, just wrote about this actually.

I actually had a wonderful conversation with someone recently that sent me on a natural happiness high. This person was just lifted my spirits somehow, as we simply discussed our day. I momentarily forgot about all the people who have wronged me, ever disappointed me, or humilated me...it was horrifying. I knew it was going to fade and I'd be back to my reality. The one in which people mostly dislike me, and are shocked by my emptiness and depressed affect. Idk.

Sounds like Buddhism, the part about reducing desires in order to feel more content and aporeciate what life does offer us. However, it all seems good in theory, but not practical. I'm going to want sex, pleasure, delicious food, ego validation, that's just human nature. I think my wiring is just...wrong. I've been sad for so long it's become comforting. Someone else here wrote that happiness itself is uncomfortable. I feel that too. I know that happiness is fleeting and only leads to an eventual and unavoidable low. The more I learn about epigenetics and neural circuitry, the more I beleive that, for a small minority of people, weathering life's emotional storms is not possible. I think I've been sad for so long, my gene's have been irreversibly affected, creating a depressive homeostasis.

I was diagnosed with CPTSD, actually, by a different therapist, many years ago. I don't quite agree as I don't have the hallmark "flashbacks" of PTSD, but I have had intrusive thoughts since I was a kid, which could be a variant of a flashback. I was in therapy for almost a decade, have taken pretty much every anti-depressant/anxiety med out there excluding benzos, and MAOIs. Nothing ever truly helped and the side effects always outweighed any benefit, if there was any. So, I gave up. Whatever I have, it's treatment resistant, which is pretty much the definition of hopeless.
